newsitem.title: UK: NatWest up, reports say reviews Markets arm.
newsitem.headline: NatWest up, reports say reviews Markets arm.

text.p: Shares in National Westminster Bank Plc rose in pre-market trade on Monday after press reports said the group was reviewing its investment banking arm NatWest Markets.
The stock was up 18-1/2p at 815p by 0729 GMT in thin trade of 46,023 shares.
A report in the Financial Times said the group was carrying out a "fundamental review" of the unit, that could lead to a scaling-back of its ambitions and the departure of its head Martin Owen.

The Sunday Times said NatWest intended to pare back the capital it had tied up in NatWest Markets, in order to focus on areas with a better potential return -- such as acquiring a life insurer. Otherwise it could return cash to shareholders, the report said.
The Sunday Times said NatWest would scale back operations such as lending to big international clients, where margins are thin, to focus on recent acquisitions such as fund manager Gartmore.
The reports follow suggestions of investor unease at the performance of NatWest, whose shares have underperformed the rampant banking sector in recent months.
Reports said NatWest would signal a change in approach at its Markets arm as it unveils a report into a 90 million stg options loss later this month.
Analysts said it was probably no surprise that NatWest markets was under review but it remained to be seen exactly what measures the bank was proposing.

"It's right that people have been screaming at them for the past 12 to 18 months that the money they have spent on acquisitions was a waste and they should have been spending it on their retail banking arm," said Ian McEwan, analyst at Lehman Brothers.
"If it's true that the operation is under review, then they are doing what people have been saying loud and clear for quite a long time," McEwan said, "but it would be a huge turnaround."
Recent speculation that NatWest had been in merger talks with Abbey National Plc was one sign that NatWest was aware of the issues it was facing, McEwan said.
